newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Pepsi's bottler BAESA loses $151.6 MLN Q4 US GAAP.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi's bottler BAESA loses $151.6 MLN Q4 US GAAP.

text.p: Argentina's Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA) announced Tuesday it posted a net loss of $151.6 million in the fourth quarter of its fiscal year 1996 ended September 30.
BAESA, the biggest Pepsi Co bottler outside the United States, told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange the result compares with a net gain of $5.4 million in the same period a year ago.
The company said it had a net loss per ADS of $4.18 in the fourth quarter against a net gain of $0.15 in the same period 1995.
In the 12 months to September 30 BAESA lost $452.4 million (a loss of $12.48 per ADS) versus a $44.8 million gain ($1.24 per ADS gain).
Results are expressed in accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (US GAAP), which may differ from those applied in Argentina.
The company announced Monday a $426.4 million loss for the year, and negative retained earnings of $323.4 million, both according to different accounting principles generally accepted in Argentina.

Fourth quarter revenues, under US GAAP, were $134.7 million vs $164.2 million and in the year $680.2 million vs $670.4 million. In the quarter BAESA had an operating loss of $148.6 million against a $13.4 million gain and in the year an operating loss of $374.3 million versus a $68.1 million gain.

In Argentina, in the quarter, net revenues fell eight percent to $70.2 million and the company had an operating loss of $23.8 million, excluding the impact of accounting adjustments and restructirng expenditures.

In Brazil, in the fourth quarter, net revenues fell 31 percent to $53.6 million and the company had an operating loss of $48.1 million, excluding the impact of accounting adjustments and restructirng expenditures.
In July Pepsi took over operating control of BAESA, which has suffered a financial crunch that many analysts blame on overexpansion.

BAESA has the exclusive Pepsi and Seven-Up franchises for the Buenos Aires Metropolitan area and other regions in Argentina, as well as Chile, Uruguay and Costa Rica and certain Southern Brazilian states, including the metropolitan areas of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
In September shareholders of BAESA filed a class action suit in Manhattan federal court against both BAESA and PEPSI alleging they hid the bottler's problems.
In October BAESA announced a standstill agreement with its leading creditors to defer until March 31 repayments of capital of about $520 million in debts.

"The standstill agreement was a first substantial step to be able to develop an integral plan of financial restructuring without which the company cannot survive," Executive Vice-President Osvaldo Banos told the Buenos Aires bolsa.
